usage: This is the standard and most common way to say 'I love you' in Moroccan Darija. The verb 'bgha' literally means 'to want', but when applied to people in this context, it translates to 'to love'. It is used between romantic partners, family members, and close friends. The suffix '-k' is gender-neutral, so it is used exactly the same way when speaking to a man or a woman.

variants.label: to a group
variants.note: Used when addressing more than one person, such as your family or a group of friends.

variants.label: emphatic
variants.note: Add 'bzaf' (a lot) to express deep affection or romantic love.

variants.label: passionate
variants.note: Literally 'I go crazy over you', used for intense romantic love or strong affection.

responses.english: May God keep you for me

examples.english: I love you so much, my life.
Do you love me or not?
